title: Artificial Intelligence in Microfinance and Financial Inclusion: Applications, Issues, and Future Directions
tldr: AI transforms microfinance and financial inclusion across payments, savings, lending, insurance, and investments, but deployment risks algorithmic bias, privacy violations, and digital exclusion without robust governance.
problem_and_motivation: Two billion adults worldwide lack access to loans, insurance, or banking services due to credit invisibility and absence from traditional credit bureaus. AI presents transformative potential for financial inclusion but carries significant risks including algorithmic bias, proxy discrimination, and digital divide exacerbation. The field lacks a systematic examination of AI applications across financial domains alongside their ethical implications for marginalized populations.
approach: Critical review of academic and gray literature combined with targeted case study analysis from the Global South.
BHAI framework adopted to evaluate humane AI development through multidimensional inclusion and ethical oversight.
Multiple purposively selected case studies of AI-driven financial services including M-Pesa, GCash, Tala, Branch, BIMA, and Pula.
Triangulation of peer-reviewed articles, working papers, and reports from World Bank, CGAP, and OECD.
Systematic mapping of AI technologies (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement learning) across five financial sectors.

definitions.definition: When individuals have no footprint in conventional credit bureaus — no credit cards, mortgages, or installment loans.
A credit file with insufficient data to generate a reliable credit score, typically requiring at least six months of credit activity.
When AI uses variables like zip code or device type that correlate with protected characteristics to make discriminatory decisions.
Building Humane Advances and Institutions — a framework advocating humane AI development through multidimensional inclusion and ethical oversight.
Coverage that pays out automatically when specific measurable events occur, such as rainfall levels or temperature thresholds.
A privacy-preserving ML approach where models are trained locally and only aggregated updates are shared.
An ensemble ML method combining multiple decision trees, with XGBoost and LightGBM dominating credit scoring production systems.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides a comprehensive critical review of AI applications across five financial sectors — payments, savings, lending, insurance, and investments — with a focus on financial inclusion for marginalized populations in the Global South. It systematically maps AI technologies (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement learning) to specific financial applications and identifies the dominant role of gradient boosting in credit scoring. The paper introduces the inclusion paradox: AI enables financial access but often at exploitative terms. It proposes the BHAI framework for humane AI development and offers technical, regulatory, and institutional recommendations for equitable deployment.

topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 4 (Landscape of Existing Personal Finance Systems, Limitations and Gaps) was flagged as high relevance since the paper comprehensively reviews AI applications across financial sectors. Domain 10 (Data Privacy and Security, User Trust) was flagged as high/medium relevance given extensive discussion of privacy violations, surveillance capitalism, and trust through transparency. Domain 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles) was flagged as medium relevance due to discussion of alternative data for behavioral profiling. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was flagged as medium relevance for its review of ML methods in credit scoring. Domain 14 (Synthetic Data) was flagged as low relevance for brief mention of GAN-based data generation. Domains 1-3, 7-9, 11-13 were considered and rejected as the paper does not specifically address Filipino demographics, culturally specific financial practices, expense categorization, budgeting strategies, mobile-first design, engagement dynamics, evaluation frameworks, or savings/debt management in personal finance systems.
